sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed; the construct was used in anthrax toxin receptor functional studies. Specific functional assay result for the tagged construct not detailed in the ledger clip.
sites.rationale: L4 explicitly states the 3xFLAG tag is placed 'immediately following the signal peptide' of full-length TEM8/ANTXR1. The signal peptide spans residues 1-32 (landmarks), so the junction is after residue 32 (R) and before residue 33 (E), the mature N-terminus. Verified computationally: residue 32 = R, residue 33 = E. The extracellular ectodomain is 289 residues long (33-321), placing this tag 289 residues from the TM boundary — well clear of any constraint. PMC3014418 (L4): Full-length human TEM8/ANTXR1 with a 3xFLAG tag incorporated onto the N-terminus immediately following the signal peptide, generated by a two-step PCR-based strategy. Construct used for surface display studies in mammalian cells.

sources.claim: A two-step PCR-based strategy was used to incorporate a 3xFLAG-tag onto the N-terminus of TEM8 immediately following the signal peptide.

(B and C) CHO ΔATR cells untransfected and stably or transiently transfected (for 48 h; B) with a TEM8/1-HA construct were analyzed by Western blotting (40 μg of protein/lane; B) or immunofluorescence (C) using an anti-HA antibody.

literature_notes: All seven ledger lines converge on a single physical junction: the extracellular N-terminus of ANTXR1/TEM8 immediately after signal peptide cleavage (after residue 32). L4 explicitly names this junction ('immediately following the signal peptide'); L1/L2/L3/L5 describe HA-tagged TEM8/1 constructs with surface confirmation but no residue stated — topology_derived to the same junction since TEM8 has only one extracellular terminus. L7 describes another 3xFLAG construct (pcDNA3.1) with no residue stated, also topology_derived to the same junction; it is subsumed by L4 (same tag, same junction, less explicit). L6 describes CMG2-V5 (ANTXR2, a paralog), not ANTXR1, and was excluded. No ledger line supports any internal loop insertion in ANTXR1. The large ectodomain (residues 33-321, 289 aa) contains the VWA domain and collagen-binding region, but no insertion within it is grounded in the ledger.
